records.name: Erzurum
records.summary:
Every province in Türkiye sits under the same intensifying national framework. A leaked draft of the 11th Judicial Package (October 2025) would criminalise LGBT conduct and advocacy — up to 3 years for behaviour 'contrary to biological sex and general morality' and 4 years for same-sex ceremonies — and would raise gender-affirming-care eligibility from 18 to 25 with a permanent-infertility mandate, exposing providers to fines and up to 7 years and patients to up to 3 years; 15 LGBT groups and the Turkish Medical Association objected. The Kaos GL 2025 human-rights report ('A Major Siege', published February 2026) finds hostility became explicit state policy in 2025 — presidency-centred, implemented through the family ministry — documenting 6 right-to-life violations including 3 hate-motivated killings with trans people most affected, 89 torture or ill-treatment cases (up from 51) and 313 liberty violations (about 2.5-fold), counted from media coverage because the state keeps no hate-crime statistics.

No province-specific ordinance, incident series or court decision concerning trans visitors in Erzurum was documented in this research pass; the national framework above is the whole documented picture for Erzurum. The absence of recorded provincial enforcement is not evidence of local tolerance, and equally not evidence of a local ban.

records.name: Isparta
records.summary:
A trans visitor in Isparta is subject to the same nationwide developments as anywhere else in the country. An October 2025 leaked omnibus draft would amend the penal code to imprison acts deemed contrary to biological sex and general morality (up to three years; up to four for same-sex ceremonies), restrict gender-affirming healthcare to people 25 and over under infertility and repeated-evaluation conditions, and expose doctors to up to seven years in prison; national monitoring reports that 2025 hostility became explicit state policy — family-year directives from the head of state, a rights organisation closed, broadcast and arts-event censorship, three hate-motivated killings, 89 torture or ill-treatment violations and a 2.5-fold rise in detentions.

No statute, incident or court case specific to Isparta appears in the surviving sources for this record: the documents behind it are national-level and carry no provincial breakdown. The absence of province-specific documentation is not evidence of local tolerance — the nationwide framework and its 2025-26 escalation reach this province as any other.

records.name: Kahramanmaraş
records.summary: No province-specific trans-related signal found in this research pass: the national framework and its 2025-26 escalation apply here unchanged. The region's sources are national-level: a leaked draft omnibus reform package (11th Judicial Package, October 2025) would create new anti-LGBT articles — criminalising conduct deemed "contrary to biological sex and general morality", restricting gender-affirming healthcare with a minimum age of 25, and enabling charges against trans people and their providers; and the state's "Year of the Family" institutional programme and blanket bans on LGBTI public events are national practice, not provincial choices. The absence of a documented provincial ban is not evidence of tolerance — the national blanket-ban practice applies across the country.
